title: Preserve mixed capability routing in evidence-gap families
objective: Fix family consolidation so an observation already classified EXISTING_REPO_DERIVATION/BACKFILL_QUEUED is not represented as UNKNOWN_SOURCE/SOURCE_DISCOVERY_REQUIRED merely because another metric in the same family is unknown. Use only existing closure semantics.
allowed_change_scope: tests directly related to evidence-gap family consolidation

evidence.summary: The family contains both EXISTING_REPO_DERIVATION/BACKFILL_QUEUED and UNKNOWN_SOURCE/SOURCE_DISCOVERY_REQUIRED observations, while family-level representation collapses the distinction.
The producer already supports derivation and source-discovery routes; the bounded defect is mixed-family consolidation.

reproduction: On fresh main, inspect EG-MARKET-STRUCTURE and confirm it contains at least one EXISTING_REPO_DERIVATION/BACKFILL_QUEUED observation and at least one UNKNOWN_SOURCE/SOURCE_DISCOVERY_REQUIRED observation. Run the current consolidation logic on an equivalent mixed-capability fixture and demonstrate that family-level output loses or obscures the per-capability routing distinction.

positive: A mixed-family fixture preserves EXISTING_REPO_DERIVATION/BACKFILL_QUEUED and UNKNOWN_SOURCE/SOURCE_DISCOVERY_REQUIRED as distinct machine-readable routes.
Current family IDs, immutable legacy observations and authority flags remain compatible.
Current EG-MARKET-STRUCTURE no longer makes derivation-capable observations appear to require source discovery solely because another observation is unknown.
negative: No new closure or policy state is introduced.
Genuinely unknown metrics remain fail-closed as SOURCE_DISCOVERY_REQUIRED.
No new source, market threshold or portfolio behavior is introduced.
Historical observations are not rewritten or deleted.

post_fix_gate: CI and mixed-capability positive and negative fixtures must pass, followed by registry readback preserving both existing route classes.
